raw_text: A 24-year-old man presents to the emergency department with 18 hours of periumbilical pain that later migrated to the right lower quadrant. He reports nausea and has not eaten since yesterday. Temperature is 38.1 C, heart rate 96/min. On examination there is tenderness at McBurney's point with rebound. White cell count is 14.2 x10^9/L with neutrophilia. The surgical team confirmed a diagnosis of acute appendicitis, also accepted as appendicitis. Mesenteric lymphadenitis was considered in the differential.

expected.title: Acute right lower quadrant pain
expected.presentation: Eighteen hours of periumbilical pain migrating to the right lower quadrant, with nausea and loss of appetite.

findings.value: Periumbilical pain migrating to the right lower quadrant
Tenderness at McBurney's point with rebound
White cell count 14.2 x10^9/L with neutrophilia

raw_text: A 41-year-old woman taking combined oral contraceptives developed sudden pleuritic chest pain and shortness of breath two days after a 12-hour flight. Heart rate is 118/min and oxygen saturation 91% on room air. Her left calf is swollen and tender. CT pulmonary angiography shows a filling defect in the right lower lobe artery. The established diagnosis is pulmonary embolism. Deep vein thrombosis was also present as a contributing differential.

expected.title: Sudden pleuritic chest pain after a long flight
expected.presentation: Sudden pleuritic chest pain and dyspnea two days after a 12-hour flight, on combined oral contraceptives.

findings.value: Sudden pleuritic chest pain and shortness of breath
CT pulmonary angiography: filling defect in the right lower lobe artery

raw_text: A 63-year-old man with a 20-year history of hypertension reports crushing substernal chest pressure radiating to the left arm for 45 minutes, with sweating. Blood pressure is 148/92 mmHg. ECG shows ST elevation in leads II, III and aVF. High-sensitivity troponin is markedly elevated at 820 ng/L. The confirmed diagnosis is inferior ST-elevation myocardial infarction, accepted as STEMI. Unstable angina was the initial consideration.

expected.title: Crushing substernal chest pressure with sweating
expected.presentation: Forty-five minutes of crushing substernal chest pressure radiating to the left arm, with diaphoresis.

findings.value: Crushing substernal chest pressure radiating to the left arm
ECG: ST elevation in leads II, III and aVF

raw_text: A 19-year-old woman is brought in with two days of vomiting, deep rapid breathing and confusion. She has lost 6 kg over three weeks and has been drinking large volumes of water. Respiratory rate is 28/min. Capillary glucose is 27 mmol/L, venous pH 7.18 and serum ketones 5.4 mmol/L. The established diagnosis is diabetic ketoacidosis, also accepted as DKA. Hyperosmolar hyperglycaemic state was excluded.

expected.title: Vomiting with deep rapid breathing and confusion
expected.presentation: Two days of vomiting, Kussmaul breathing and confusion, following three weeks of weight loss and polydipsia.

findings.value: 6 kg weight loss over three weeks

raw_text: A 72-year-old man presents with fever, productive cough with rust-coloured sputum and right-sided pleuritic pain for three days. He has smoked for 40 years. Temperature is 38.9 C and respiratory rate 24/min. There are crackles and dullness to percussion over the right lower lobe. Chest radiograph shows right lower lobe consolidation. CRP is 180 mg/L. The confirmed diagnosis is community-acquired pneumonia, also accepted as lobar pneumonia. Pulmonary tuberculosis was considered.

expected.title: Fever with productive cough and pleuritic pain
expected.presentation: Three days of fever, productive cough with rust-coloured sputum and right-sided pleuritic chest pain.

findings.value: Crackles and dullness to percussion over the right lower lobe
Chest radiograph: right lower lobe consolidation

raw_text: A 34-year-old woman reports the worst headache of her life, which began abruptly while lifting weights, with vomiting and neck stiffness. Blood pressure is 162/95 mmHg. Neck flexion is painful and photophobia is present; there is no focal weakness. Non-contrast CT of the head shows blood in the basal cisterns. The established diagnosis is subarachnoid haemorrhage. Bacterial meningitis was in the differential.

expected.title: Abrupt worst-ever headache with neck stiffness
expected.presentation: Abrupt onset of the worst headache of her life during exertion, with vomiting and neck stiffness.

findings.value: Painful neck flexion without focal weakness
Non-contrast head CT: blood in the basal cisterns

raw_text: A 58-year-old woman with gallstones presents with severe epigastric pain radiating to the back, relieved by leaning forward, with repeated vomiting for one day. Heart rate is 104/min and temperature 37.8 C. The epigastrium is tender with guarding. Serum lipase is 1420 U/L and ALT 180 U/L. Abdominal ultrasound shows gallstones with a dilated common bile duct. The confirmed diagnosis is acute gallstone pancreatitis, accepted as acute pancreatitis. Perforated peptic ulcer was excluded.

expected.title: Severe epigastric pain radiating to the back
expected.presentation: One day of severe epigastric pain radiating to the back, relieved by leaning forward, with repeated vomiting.

findings.value: Epigastric pain radiating to the back, relieved by leaning forward
Abdominal ultrasound: gallstones with a dilated common bile duct

raw_text: A 29-year-old man reports one week of burning retrosternal pain after meals and at night, with an acid taste in the mouth. He drinks four cups of coffee daily and takes no regular medications. Examination and vital signs are unremarkable; no epigastric tenderness is found. Upper endoscopy shows grade A oesophagitis. The established diagnosis is gastro-oesophageal reflux disease, accepted as GERD. Peptic ulcer disease was considered and not found.

expected.title: Burning retrosternal pain after meals
expected.presentation: One week of burning retrosternal pain after meals and at night, with acid regurgitation.

findings.value: Burning retrosternal pain after meals and at night

raw_text: A 46-year-old woman reports six weeks of fatigue, cold intolerance, constipation and a 4 kg weight gain. Her mother has autoimmune thyroid disease. Heart rate is 54/min. The thyroid is diffusely firm and non-tender; ankle reflexes are delayed. TSH is 18.4 mIU/L with free T4 of 8.1 pmol/L and positive anti-TPO antibodies. The confirmed diagnosis is Hashimoto thyroiditis, accepted as autoimmune hypothyroidism. Iodine deficiency was considered unlikely.

expected.title: Fatigue with cold intolerance and weight gain
expected.presentation: Six weeks of fatigue, cold intolerance, constipation and 4 kg weight gain.

findings.value: 4 kg weight gain over six weeks
Diffusely firm, non-tender thyroid with delayed ankle reflexes
TSH 18.4 mIU/L with free T4 8.1 pmol/L

raw_text: A patient of unstated age and sex presents with three days of dysuria, urinary frequency and left flank pain, with one episode of shaking chills. Temperature is 38.6 C and there is left costovertebral angle tenderness. Urinalysis shows pyuria with positive nitrites, and urine culture grew Escherichia coli at 10^5 CFU/mL. The established diagnosis is acute pyelonephritis. Uncomplicated cystitis was the initial differential.

expected.title: Dysuria with flank pain and fever
expected.presentation: Three days of dysuria, urinary frequency and left flank pain with rigors.

findings.value: Left flank pain with shaking chills
